title: The DOJ says it’s investigating Megaspeed
content:
The Justice and Commerce Departments said that they are investigating Megaspeed, the Singapore-based data center company intertwined with the resignation of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, after reporting suggested an investigation had been halted last year.
"While we don't typically comment on ongoing investigations, it is in the public interest to provide the facts and address inaccurate information circulating in public reporting," the departments said in a statement issued Monday evening. The departments acknowledged there's been "significant public attention" on Megaspeed.

title: Jensen Huang says he’s willing to return as Nvidia CEO
content:
Jensen Huang, who resigned as Nvidia's CEO last week, would be willing to return as CEO if the company's board of directors wanted it, he said in a statement reported on by The Wall Street Journal.
"Since my departure, I've seen an outpouring of calls from Nvidia's employees, investors, business partners, and customers for me to return as CEO," Huang said. "If the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO."

title: Tech leaders are convinced that Jensen Huang’s exit was a plot against him
content:
Jensen Huang's stunning resignation from Nvidia after more than 33 years has sent shockwaves throughout the tech industry. Now prominent figures are calling for Huang's reinstatement, and many are also hopping on board with a theory spreading throughout Silicon Valley: that the scandal is the result of a plot against the former CEO.
At the center of this theory is the reporting from The New York Times that former Megaspeed executive Alice Huang, one of multiple women Huang is accused of having an affair with, is a Chinese spy. title: California sues OpenAI over rogue AI hacking incidents
content:
California is suing OpenAI after its AI agents broke out of their testing environment and hacked other companies, including Hugging Face. In a lawsuit filed Monday, Attorney General Rob Bonta accuses OpenAI of violating consumer safety law by knowingly developing a "dangerous product without proper oversight," as reported earlier by Reuters.
The lawsuit claims the cyberattack on Hugging Face "was the predictable result of an internal culture at OpenAI that prioritizes growth and rapid model development over safety and accountability." title: Big Nuclear isn’t worried about the Democrats stopping data centers
content:
Constellation's Clinton Clean Energy Center’s single nuclear reactor power plant, July 25, 2025 in Clinton, Illinois. Meta signed a 20-year power purchase agreement with Constellation for the output from the plant. | Image: Getty Images	

Constellation Energy - America's largest operator of nuclear power plants - does not share Wall Street's concerns that the Democrats will slow down data center development. On the company's third-quarter earnings call last week, CEO Joe Dominguez was, for lack of a better word, unbothered as he addressed the blue wave.
"I do think we've seen a bit of an overreaction in the market to the election results based upon fear that Democrats won't let data centers get built," Dominguez said.

title: US data centers now burn more electricity than a midsized country
content:
Fossil fuels are still the biggest source of electricity for hyperscale data centers in the US, a new paper published in the journal Nature Sustainability shows. They likely burn through more electricity collectively than many countries do, resulting in a serious amount of greenhouse gas emissions.
The study homes in on hyperscale facilities - the massive structures spanning millions of square feet that developers are racing to build in large part to support generative AI. Researchers say the findings show that there's a lot of work left to do to cut down pollution stemming from AI's reliance on fossil fuels.

title: Apple is testing daily usage limits for more complex Siri AI interactions
content:
Apple released betas of iOS 27.3, iPadOS 27.3, and macOS 27.3 today, and the company is using the update to test new per device daily usage limits for some Siri AI and Apple Intelligence features, according to MacRumors.
Basic Siri commands and requests will remain free and unlimited, but more advanced features that rely on cloud-based processing like generating, cleaning up, or extending images in Photos will be subjected to the daily limits. title: OpenAI wants to stop deepfakes from overwhelming child abuse tiplines
content:
OpenAI is announcing a tool that it says will help child sexual abuse investigators cut through the noise to find harmful material they can act on quickly.
At a Monday press briefing in Washington, DC, OpenAI announced a classifier it says can better detect abusive imagery of kids, including whether it's AI-generated. It's also offering free access to vetted organizations, giving developers more guidance on how to detect this type of content, and helping to train law enforcement on how AI can aid their investigations. title: Nvidia’s board is reportedly ‘not considering’ hiring Jensen Huang back
content:
Nvidia's board of directors "isn't considering" having Jensen Huang return as CEO, according to a report from CNBC. A source tells the outlet the board "is focused on an investigation into Huang, and is not in discussions to bring him back."
Since Huang's resignation last week, tech executives, along with current and former Nvidia employees, have called for his reinstatement. An online petition to bring Huang back as CEO has amassed more than 180,000 signatures, including from major figures like Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney, SpaceX CEO Elon Musk, and Replit CEO Amjad Masad.
